quests.instruction: "Waving to the mail carrier delivering letters" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when mail carriers usually walk their delivery routes.
quests.explanation: Yes! Mail is delivered while streets and homes are easy to see.
quests.funFact: Mail carriers in some places walk many miles every single day!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Streetlights turning on along the road"?
quests.hint: Think about when streetlights are needed to help people see outside.
quests.explanation: Yes! Streetlights turn on to light up the dark road.
quests.funFact: Streetlights use a light sensor to turn on by themselves when it gets dark!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A dog chasing a ball in the backyard"?
quests.hint: Think about when pets usually get taken outside to play and run.
quests.explanation: Yes! Playing fetch outside is a fun activity for dogs and their families.
quests.funFact: Dogs can see some colors, but not as many as people can!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Closing the curtains before climbing into bed". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about what we close over the window to make the room dark for sleeping.
quests.explanation: Yes! We close the curtains to help make the room dark and cozy for sleep.
quests.funFact: Some curtains are made extra thick just to block out all outside light!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Picking ripe apples from a tree". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when farmers and families go outside to harvest fruit.
quests.explanation: Yes! Picking fruit is outdoor work best done while it's light outside.
quests.funFact: An apple tree can take up to ten years to grow its very first apples!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Letting out a big, sleepy yawn"?
quests.hint: Think about what your body does when it starts feeling tired and ready for bed.
quests.explanation: Yes! We yawn when we feel sleepy, especially before bed.
quests.funFact: Yawning might actually help cool down your brain, say some scientists!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Jumping rope with friends at recess"?
quests.hint: Think about the short break during the school day when kids play outside.
quests.explanation: Yes! Recess is a playtime break during the school day.
quests.funFact: Jumping rope is a great way to build strong muscles and good balance!

quests.instruction: "Counting sheep to help fall asleep" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about the old trick some people use to help their mind get sleepy.
quests.explanation: Yes! Counting sheep is an old trick people use to help them fall asleep.
quests.funFact: This sleepy trick has been used in stories for hundreds of years!

quests.instruction: "A farmer driving a tractor through the field" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when farmers usually do most of their outdoor work.
quests.explanation: Yes! Farmers do most of their fieldwork during daylight hours.
quests.funFact: Some modern tractors can even drive themselves using satellites!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The whole house growing quiet and still"?
quests.hint: Think about how a busy house sounds once everyone goes to sleep.
quests.explanation: Yes! Homes get quiet and still once everyone is asleep.
quests.funFact: Quiet, calm spaces can help our bodies and minds rest more deeply!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Bees buzzing busily around a flower". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when bees are usually out collecting pollen.
quests.explanation: Yes! Bees are busy collecting pollen from flowers during the day.
quests.funFact: A single bee visits about 50 to 100 flowers on just one trip!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A raccoon searching for food in the dark". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about the masked animal known for exploring after dark.
quests.explanation: Yes! Raccoons are nocturnal and search for food at night.
quests.funFact: A raccoon's clever front paws work almost like tiny human hands!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Having a picnic under a shady tree"?
quests.hint: Think about when families usually pack a lunch to eat outside.
quests.explanation: Yes! Picnics are a fun outdoor meal enjoyed in the daylight.
quests.funFact: The word 'picnic' comes from an old French word for a shared outdoor meal!

quests.instruction: "Fireworks bursting and lighting up the sky" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when fireworks show up brightest against a dark sky.
quests.explanation: Yes! Fireworks are best seen at night, when the dark sky makes their colors pop.
quests.funFact: Fireworks get their bright colors from special metal powders mixed inside them!

quests.instruction: "Washing the car in the driveway" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when it's easiest to see the dirt and soap while cleaning.
quests.explanation: Yes! Washing a car outside is easiest to do while it's light out.
quests.funFact: A garden hose can spray enough water to fill a small pool in just a few minutes!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Putting on warm, fuzzy slippers before bed"?
quests.hint: Think about the soft shoes people wear around the house before sleeping.
quests.explanation: Yes! Fuzzy slippers are often worn while getting cozy before bed.
quests.funFact: Slippers help keep your feet warm on cold floors at night!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A colorful rainbow appearing after the rain"?
quests.hint: Think about what you need in the sky to see a rainbow: sunlight!
quests.explanation: Yes! Rainbows form when sunlight shines through raindrops, so they appear in the daytime.
quests.funFact: A rainbow is actually a full circle, but we usually only see half of it!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A soft lullaby playing quietly". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about the gentle, sleepy song a parent might sing at bedtime.
quests.explanation: Yes! Lullabies are gentle songs sung to help little ones fall asleep.
quests.funFact: Lullabies have been sung to babies in every culture around the world for centuries!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Feeding the ducks at the pond". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when families usually take a walk to visit a pond.
quests.explanation: Yes! Feeding ducks at the park is a relaxing outdoor activity.
quests.funFact: Ducks have waterproof feathers that keep them dry while they swim!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Switching off the bedroom light"?
quests.hint: Think about the very last thing you do before closing your eyes to sleep.
quests.explanation: Yes! We turn off the light right before falling asleep.
quests.funFact: A dark room can actually help your body know it's time to rest!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Skipping smooth stones across a lake"?
quests.hint: Think about when it's easiest to see the stones splash on the water.
quests.explanation: Yes! It's easiest to skip stones and watch them splash while it's light out.
quests.funFact: The world record for skipping a stone is over 80 skips in a row!

quests.instruction: "Laying out clothes for the morning before bed" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when families sometimes get ready early for the next busy day.
quests.explanation: Yes! Getting things ready for tomorrow is a calm habit before bed.
quests.funFact: Planning ahead like this can make busy mornings feel much less rushed!

quests.instruction: "A crossing guard helping children cross the street" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when children are walking to and from school.
quests.explanation: Yes! Crossing guards help children get to school safely during school hours.
quests.funFact: Crossing guards wear bright colors so drivers can spot them easily!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Looking through a telescope at the stars". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about the special tool used to see faraway stars up close.
quests.explanation: Yes! Telescopes are used at night to get a closer look at the stars and moon.
quests.funFact: Some telescopes are so powerful they can see galaxies far beyond our own!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Planting seeds in the garden soil". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when gardeners usually go outside to plant.
quests.explanation: Yes! Planting seeds is outdoor garden work done in the daylight.
quests.funFact: Some tiny seeds can grow into plants that are taller than a house!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A moth fluttering around a porch light"?
quests.hint: Think about the small flying insect that's drawn to bright lights after dark.
quests.explanation: Yes! Moths are usually most active at night, often fluttering near lights.
quests.funFact: Scientists think moths may follow the moon to help them fly straight at night!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Blowing bubbles in the backyard"?
quests.hint: Think about when it's easiest to watch bubbles float and sparkle in the light.
quests.explanation: Yes! Bubbles sparkle best in sunlight, so this is a fun outdoor activity.
quests.funFact: A bubble's rainbow colors come from light bouncing inside its thin, soapy walls!

quests.instruction: "The glowing moon slowly changing its shape, a little more each time we see it" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about how the moon in the sky looks a little different each time you spot it.
quests.explanation: Yes! We watch the moon's changing shape at night, as it moves through its phases.
quests.funFact: It takes about a month for the moon to go through all of its different shapes!

quests.instruction: "Putting on sunscreen before going outside to play" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when your skin needs protection from strong sunlight.
quests.explanation: Yes! We wear sunscreen to protect our skin while the sun is out.
quests.funFact: Sunscreen was invented to help people enjoy the outdoors without getting sunburned!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Setting an alarm clock before falling asleep"?
quests.hint: Think about when we prepare the clock that will wake us up tomorrow.
quests.explanation: Yes! We set an alarm clock at night, getting ready for the next morning.
quests.funFact: The very first alarm clocks could only ring at one single time, not any time you wanted!
